title: Finite etale extension across a regular codimension-two boundary
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme, and $V\subseteq L$ an open subset. Suppose that for every $z\notin V$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{L,z}$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] and has Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] at least two. For every finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] morphism $q:Y\to V$, there is a finite etale morphism $p:E\to L$ and an isomorphism $e:Y\cong E\times_L V$ over $V$; explicitly, $e\circ p|_V=q$. No global quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BMA (pione-lemma-purity-regular); Tag 0EY7 (pione-lemma-purity-essentially-surjective); Tag 0H2W (final paragraph of the locally Noetherian extension theorem); Tag 0EY6(2), uniqueness by the depth-two extension identity

proof.text: A missing point has a regular local ring of dimension at least two, so purity holds for its punctured spectrum by 0BMA. The open V contains all generic and codimension-one points, since the dimension bound excludes them from the complement.

On each Noetherian affine open, extend the finite etale cover by 0EY7: at a generic point of a component of the missing closed subset its local inverse image is the punctured spectrum; use local purity, spread the extension to a larger open, and continue by Noetherian induction. This is the final extension step used in 0H2W.

On overlaps the finite etale algebras are finite locally free. At each missing point the regular local ring has depth equal to its dimension, at least two, and the algebras as modules have the same depth bound. The depth-two extension identity identifies each algebra with the direct image of its restriction to V, as in 0EY6(2). Thus the given algebra isomorphism over V extends uniquely on overlaps. Uniqueness gives the cocycle condition, so descent glues the extensions and their isomorphism over V. Empty covers extend by the empty cover.
